# Street Code: a field guide to every mark, box, cap and sign on a city street

> A cited field guide to everything on a city street: spray paint colors, hydrant caps, manhole covers, road lines, pole hardware, sign codes, curbs and sidewalk stamps.

A cited field guide (345 sources, about 44,885 words) to everything visible on a city street and what it means: utility locate paint colors and 811, survey marks and benchmarks, fire hydrant colors and fire department connections, fire alarm boxes, manhole covers and their inscriptions, valve boxes, storm drain markers and vault lights, road line colors and patterns, crosswalks and bike lanes, what is on a utility pole, traffic signal hardware and cameras, sign shapes, colors, fonts and codes, curb colors, curb ramps and tactile paving, sidewalk stamps and street archaeology, work zones and utility cabinets. Boston is the worked example.

## Key facts
- What do the colored spray paint marks on my lawn mean? They are locate marks showing roughly where buried utilities run, painted after someone requested a locate before digging. Red is electric, orange communications, yellow gas or oil, blue drinking water, green sewer, purple reclaimed water, pink survey marks and white the proposed dig area. The paint and flags do not cause long-term harm to a lawn.
- What does white paint on the sidewalk mean before digging? White marks outline where an excavator plans to dig, so locators know which lines to mark. In Massachusetts this premarking is required before any excavation, even on private property, and before calling Dig Safe.
- What does "NO" spray painted on the ground mean? It is a no-conflict mark: the named owner checked and has no facilities in the dig area. CGA guidance is NO plus the owner's identifier in its utility color, such as NO TELCO. It speaks only for that owner.
- What do the colors on fire hydrants mean? Under the voluntary NFPA 291 recommendation, the top and caps show flow: light blue 1,500 GPM or more, green 1,000 to 1,499, orange 500 to 999, red under 500. The body shows the supply: yellow for municipal, red for private, violet for non-potable water. Most cities do not follow the scheme exactly.
- What do blue reflectors in the road mean? A blue raised pavement marker is sometimes placed in the road to help fire crews find a hydrant at night. The MUTCD allows it but does not require it, and it is most common where there is no snowplowing.
- Why are manhole covers round? There is no single answer, according to Live Science. A round cover cannot fall through its own opening, can be rolled, and fits round openings cut with rotating tools. The question became famous as a Microsoft interview prompt.
- What does BWSC on a manhole cover mean? BWSC is the Boston Water and Sewer Commission, created in 1977. Older Boston water covers read BWW, for Boston Water Works.
- What is the difference between yellow and white lines on the road? In the US, yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mark the left edge of one-way roads and divided highways. White lines separate traffic moving the same direction and mark the right edge of the road.
- What is the round brass disk in the sidewalk? It is a survey mark, usually a brass or aluminum disk about 3.5 in. across, stamped with a station name, year and agency. Many were set by the National Geodetic Survey or the US Coast and Geodetic Survey, and removing one is a federal offense.
- How do I look up a survey benchmark? Each NGS mark has a six-character PID; its datasheet gives coordinates, elevation and directions from landmarks. Anyone can report a found mark through the NGS Mark Recovery Form.
- What was that loud bang from the power pole during the storm? It is often a fuse cutout operating, not a transformer exploding. A fuse melts when current becomes unsafe, the barrel swings open and power is cut, isolating the problem, according to Indiana Connection.
- What is the blue light on top of a traffic light? It is usually a red-light confirmation light that turns on with the red so officers can see violations from a safe spot. Bismarck, ND says these lights do not use automated photography.
- Why does the crosswalk button tick? The tick is the locator tone of an accessible pedestrian signal, repeating once per second so blind pedestrians can find the button. During WALK it changes to a rapid tick, a different tone or speech, and the raised arrow vibrates.
- Why are stop signs octagons? A national committee chose the octagon in 1922 so drivers could recognize a stop sign by shape alone, even from behind. The US MUTCD reserves the octagon exclusively for stop signs.
- What does a pink road sign mean? Fluorescent pink is the US background color for incident management signs, the temporary signs used at crashes and other emergencies. Orange is used for planned work zones.
- What do the stickers on the back of road signs mean? They are inventory labels that record details such as the reflective sheeting maker, fabricator and dates of fabrication and installation. Texas DOT, for example, has required a punch-coded decal on signs installed after August 15, 1980, to track how materials hold up.
- Why are there yellow bumps on the sidewalk? They are detectable warning surfaces made of truncated domes, which tell blind and low-vision pedestrians that the sidewalk is ending at a street or drop-off. Yellow gives high contrast for people with partial sight; US federal rules require contrast, and California requires yellow.
- What do the different curb colors mean? In California, Vehicle Code 21458 sets the code: red is no stopping, yellow is loading or unloading passengers or freight, white is passenger loading or mail drop, green is time-limited parking and blue is disabled parking. Local ordinances set the hours. New York State's manual says colored curbs shall not be used to convey parking rules, so read the signs.
- Why is the nut on a fire hydrant a pentagon? Ordinary wrenches and sockets fit square or hex nuts, so a five-sided nut keeps people without a hydrant wrench from opening it. Unauthorized opening wastes water and lowers the pressure firefighters need.
- Why do drain grates have bars going sideways? Long slots running with traffic can catch a bicycle wheel. In 1980 the FHWA recommended three bicycle-safe designs with transverse rods, spacers or curved vanes.
- What are the purple glass circles in the sidewalk? They are vault lights, glass lenses that let daylight into the space under the sidewalk, patented by Thaddeus Hyatt in 1845. They turn purple because manganese in the glass reacts to ultraviolet light over decades.
- What does the metal tag on a utility pole mean? The brand shows the pole's class, height, maker, species, treatment and date. In Ameren's system, oval tags show inspection years, red and yellow tags mark replacement priority, and orange tape marks a reinforced pole.
- What does a flashing yellow arrow mean? It means you may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. It was formally authorized in the federal MUTCD in 2009.
- What font is used on highway signs? Most US road signs use the FHWA Standard Alphabets, nicknamed Highway Gothic, first published in 1948. Some guide signs use Clearview, an optional typeface whose federal approval was terminated in 2016 and reinstated in 2018.
- Why are bike lanes painted green? Green pavement highlights bike space, mainly where bikes and cars cross paths. It was allowed from April 15, 2011 under FHWA Interim Approval IA-14 and is now part of the MUTCD 11th edition.
- Do Boston fire alarm boxes still work? Yes. As of April 2026 Boston had about 1,250 street boxes in service, which send their number by telegraph to the Fire Alarm Office on the Fenway. They were used during 911 outages in 2018 and 2024.
- Is every intersection a crosswalk? In most US states, yes: the Uniform Vehicle Code defines a crosswalk at an intersection as the extension of the sidewalk across the road whether or not it is marked. A midblock crosswalk exists only where it is painted, and definitions vary by state.
